subject: Sierra2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer impact and recovery commitments
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@greenfield.ai>, ops@greenfield.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: SRE: Sierra2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — immediate mitigation

Sarah / Greenfield ops team —

We’re seeing a spike in 5xx and generation timeouts originating from the Sierra2B fleet in us-west-2 starting ~16:50 PDT. Impact: approximately 6–8% of generation requests to the sierra2b model are returning 5xx or timing out (95th pct latency > 2s). We’ve already taken the following actions: 

- Rolled a configuration rollback to previous kernel selection (rolled back the experimental kernel patch) at 16:58 PDT.
- Enabled automatic model-fallbacks: your production routing now directs new requests to sierra2b-quant and sierra2b-replica pools where compatible.
- Applied a temporary rate cap per-API-key to reduce queueing for affected workers.

We suspect the issue is related to a kernel-level memory growth for long-context KV cache on the new optimization path; engineering is investigating.

Immediate asks for Greenfield.ai: if you see requests still failing, please share a small sample request_ids (up to 20) and the timestamps so we can correlate logs. We’ll compile an incident timeline and send an update within 3 hours and again by 09:00 PDT tomorrow.

Attachments: incident timeline stub attached (sierra2b_incident_timeline.csv)

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize a rollback if impact continues.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@greenfield.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@greenfield.ai, Gabe Morales <gabe@cloudbuy.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 18:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: SRE: Sierra2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — immediate mitigation

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick note and for enabling the fallback. We saw a correlated uptick in error rates on our side for ~16:55–17:10, primarily affecting streaming endpoints for short-answer flows. The fallback helped, but we still have intermittent errors for ~2% of requests (some of these are high-value transactions).

Requested: can you confirm whether the rate cap is per-key or per-deployment? Also, please share the MOP for rolling back the kernel so our platform team understands the window and any expected latency blips.

We’ll pull request_ids and send over sensitive samples via the secure form (ops@greenfield.ai will upload).

Appreciate the transparency — we’re happy to join a short call if that helps.

—Sarah
Head of Platform, Greenfield.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@greenfield.ai>, ops@greenfield.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 02:22:13 -0700
Subject: RE: SRE: Sierra2B elevated 5xx/timeouts — immediate mitigation

Team / Sarah —

Quick ops update and preliminary RCA (working draft):

Timeline (high level):
- 16:39 PDT: Canary kernel rollout (optimized attention kernel v2) begins across sierra2b canaries (small percent).
- 16:50 PDT: First 5xx spike observed in canaries; increased error rates detected by alerting.
- 16:58 PDT: We rolled back kernel selection for all sierra2b canaries; started routing traffic to sierra2b-quant and sierra2b-replica.
- 17:06 PDT: Autoscaling triggered extra workers; we observed increased queue wait times while workers warmed.

Root cause hypothesis: a regression in the new kernel led to unbounded growth of the KV cache reference counts for a subset of request patterns (long-chat, frequent prefix reuse). This caused memory pressure and intermittent task failures on affected GPUs, yielding 5xx and timeouts.

Mitigations completed: rollback to prior kernel, enabled fallbacks, per-key rate cap, and live GC-assisted cache purge on a subset of hosts.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Revert kernel changes in mainline until the kernel regression is fixed and bench-tested against long-chat traces (ETA: 48 hours)
- Add a hard memory ceiling for KV caches and an early-fail path to avoid task-level OOMs (ETA: 72 hours)
- Expand canary test coverage to include long-context traces that match customer production distributions (ETA: 1 week)

Customer communications: we’re preparing a short customer-facing recovery note and a full postmortem that will include impact, timeline, and credits where appropriate. Draft postmortem is at: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1X_Sierra2B_Postmortem (draft). We’ll circulate the final RCA within two business days.

Attachments: sierra2b_rca_draft.docx (timeline + initial logs)

Rishi
Sr. SRE Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Sierra2B incident: recovery confirmed and next steps

Hi Sarah / Greenfield team —

Update and commitments following last night’s Sierra2B degradation: 

What happened (short): a kernel regression caused KV-cache memory growth on a subset of Sierra2B workers which produced elevated 5xx and timeouts for some customers between ~16:50–17:15 PDT on 2027-07-27. We rolled back the kernel, activated fallback pools, and applied temporary rate caps to stabilize traffic.

What we did for you: 
- Your traffic was shifted to sierra2b-quant and replica pools within ~8 minutes of detection; error rate reduced to baseline by 17:12 PDT.
- We’ve applied a tailored per-key soft rate cap for your account to prevent burst queueing while we finalize the root-cause fix (will not change token quotas).
- We are providing a goodwill credit of 10% for the impacted hour(s) on your July invoice; billing team is preparing a formal credit memo.

Next steps and timelines: 
- Final RCA and postmortem (with timeline, impact table, and mitigation details): will be published by EOD tomorrow. Link (draft): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1X_Sierra2B_Postmortem
- Permanent fixes: revert the kernel from mainline (48h) + memory ceiling + expanded canaries (72h–1 week). We will post updates in the linked doc and notify you of any maintenance that might affect latency.
- Follow-up: I’ll set up a short 30-minute sync this week with our runtime and Greenfield platform teams to walk the RCA and confirm your rollout preferences. Proposed slots: Thu 09:00–11:00 PDT or Fri 13:00–15:00 PDT — please let me know which works.

If you want additional context earlier, Rishi and Marissa are on the thread and can jump on a call.

Thanks again for the patience — we know reliability is critical for your flows.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
